subject: System Design
title: Stateless vs Stateful Services
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stateless vs Stateful Services.

hook.text: A stateless server treats every request as brand new. A stateful one remembers your previous requests.

buildup.text: Stateless services store no user data locally. Any server can handle any request.

discovery.text: This makes scaling trivial: just add more servers behind a load balancer.

twist.text: Stateful services like WebSocket servers need sticky sessions, making them harder to scale and replace.

climax.text: Making services stateless is one of the most impactful decisions for scalability.

quiz.question: Why are stateless services easier to scale?
options: Any server can handle any request
